key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 strongly tunes bandgap and photovoltaic performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the most promising solar absorber.
engineering_relevance: The results identify composition control as a practical design lever for optimizing perovskite-inspired materials for next-generation photovoltaic devices.
method: First-principles calculations of structural and electronic properties
Optical property analysis to assess light-absorption potential
SLME screening to estimate solar cell efficiency
evidence_signal: All four compounds were predicted to have direct bandgaps (2.0–3.788 eV), and SLME ranked Ca3PI3 highest at 29.6% while Ca3PF3 was lowest at 0.6%.
watch_item: The reported efficiencies come from computational screening, so experimental stability, synthesis feasibility, and device integration still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
